methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Foundation Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Sankaet Pathak, Arjun Sethi, and Mike LeBlanc. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public company, including peers such as Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics across Series B and Seed stages.

Two triangulation methods anchor the analysis. Stage-progression methodology applies a 2.0x multiplier to the company's $50M total raised, implying a $100M valuation. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $2.0B. The peer set includes Generalist AI at $2.0B (Series B), Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B (Series B), Dexterity at $1.6B (Series B), and Walden Robotics at $1.1B (Seed).

The triangulated valuation range is $85M to $2.0B, with a median of $900M. The significant spread reflects material uncertainty around stage-appropriate comparability: stage-progression conservatively implies $100M, while peer multiples suggest substantially higher value. Resolution hinges on whether Foundation Robotics' technology, commercial traction, and capital efficiency justify Series B+ valuations relative to the peer cohort, or whether earlier-stage discounting applies. The reported $3B+ target for a $500M raise sits above the high end of this analysis.
